etymology: Jared Diamond's term for change that arrives in increments too small to object to, each one accepted because the last one was.
committed_when: The next step is being justified by the size of the step rather than the direction of the walk.
tell: Every individual change is small, defensible and already done; only the sequence is indefensible.
counter: Ask what the total is, not what the increment is. A series can be refused where a step cannot.
senses: Accepting each small change because it is small, so that a large one gets assembled out of pieces nobody had to defend: the fee, then the surcharge, then the surcharge with the waiting period.
It works because objection has a fixed cost and every increment is smaller than that cost. The room is never wrong about any single step; it is only never asked about the direction.
example: *"Nobody voted to end public comment."* The period went from thirty days to ten, then to "as practicable", then to a form that closed on Fridays.

confused_with.tell: The slippery slope is a prediction made by someone arguing against the first step; creeping normality is the same walk recorded afterwards by someone who did not notice it.
